summary: Updates RFC 3326 so a SIP message can carry multiple Reason header field values for the same protocol, when that protocol defines what multiple values mean. The original rule allowed only one value per protocol.

plainLanguage.summary: A note explaining why a call ended used to allow one reason per category. Now it may list several when the category says how to read them.

questions: can sip have more than one reason header
what is the sip reason header
can a sip message have multiple reason headers
what does rfc 9366 change in rfc 3326
subtitle: A SIP message may now carry several Reason values for one protocol, if that protocol says what that means.

tldr.problem: RFC 3326 allowed only one Reason header field value per protocol value, but experience with newer protocols shows that several values with the same protocol value are useful.
tldr.mechanism: The last paragraph of Section 2 of RFC 3326 is replaced: more than one value for a registered protocol MAY be present if that protocol specifies what multiple values mean; otherwise there MUST be only one value per protocol.
tldr.outcome: It updates RFC 3326 and leaves the one-value limit in place for protocols that do not define the meaning of multiple values.

today: RFC 9366 is a Proposed Standard published in March 2023. It updates RFC 3326 and has not been obsoleted or updated.

sections.title: The Problem with One Value
sections.content:
The SIP Reason header field, defined in RFC 3326, allows only one Reason value per protocol value. More recently defined protocols have shown that it is useful to allow multiple values with the same protocol value. The RFC cites a STIR draft on identity header error handling as that experience.

This document does not change the requirement in RFC 3326 restricting the header field to one value per protocol for protocols that do not define what multiple values mean.
sections.plainLanguage: The old rule said each kind of reason could be listed once. Some newer kinds needed to list more than one.

sections.title: The Replacement Text
sections.content:
The last paragraph of Section 2 of RFC 3326 is replaced. The old text said all Reason values in a message MUST have different protocol values. The new text says a message MAY contain more than one Reason value (multiple Reason lines).

If the registered protocol for the Reason value specifies what it means for multiple values to occur in one message, more than one value for that protocol MAY be present. Otherwise there MUST be only one value per protocol, for example one SIP and another Q.850. An implementation is still free to ignore Reason values that it does not understand.
sections.plainLanguage: Several reasons of one kind are fine only if that kind's own rules say how to read them. If not, keep to one of each kind.

sections.title: Security and IANA
sections.content: The document adds no security considerations to the use of SIP. The security considerations in RFC 3326 and those of any registered protocols used in Reason header field values should be considered. It has no IANA actions.
sections.plainLanguage: Nothing new to worry about. Follow the safety notes of the old rule and of each reason kind.
